How a project works · Relevant experience

Plant network work

Operational technology (OT) includes systems that monitor and control physical equipment. Our network services focus on the connections those systems use.

Installation and Equipment Connections

Network equipment installation and connections for production areas, including operator screens (HMIs) and programmable logic controllers (PLCs).

Communication Troubleshooting

Investigation of dropped or unreliable connections between devices. Testing and access are agreed around the equipment and production requirements.

Redundancy and Documentation

Support for Parallel Redundancy Protocol (PRP) networks, which use two communication paths, along with network drawings, equipment lists, and connection records.

What to include in your inquiry

  • The affected equipment and the symptoms or planned change
  • Your site location and preferred timing
  • Whether production is affected and any available maintenance window
  • The IT, maintenance, and equipment-vendor contacts involved

A high-level description is enough to begin. We agree on how to exchange technical records after discussing the project.

Assessment and implementation

An investigation produces findings and recommended actions. Installation or configuration changes require an agreed implementation scope. The handover includes the records, checks, and open items defined for that work.

BEFORE WORK STARTS

Plan around the equipment and the people who run it.

Coordinate

Agree on authorized changes, site requirements, work windows, and the roles of your IT team, maintenance staff, and equipment vendors.

Test

Define the checks needed to confirm the result, who reviews them, and when production can resume after any agreed interruption.

Prepare for recovery

Identify the records, configurations, and vendor support needed to restore the previous setup if a change does not pass its checks.

Common Questions

Does this include programming our machines?

This page covers industrial network connectivity. Changes to control programs, machine behavior, or electrical systems are not implied by a network project and require separate scope and appropriate expertise.

Can you guarantee there will be no downtime?

No. We discuss interruption risks and agree on work windows, testing, and recovery arrangements before changes. The requirements depend on your equipment and the proposed work.

Can we bring in our existing IT provider or machine vendor?

Yes. Identify those contacts during planning so responsibilities, approvals, and any vendor-dependent work can be agreed.
